This paper presents a systematic empirical comparison of five LLM augmentation strategies applied to document-grounded question answering over a corpus of academic research documents: (1) Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) with FAISS vector search and bibliography filtering, (2) Knowledge Graph (KG) augmentation using NetworkX-based co-occurrence graphs, (3) a Multi-Step Reasoning Agent employing iterative plan-searchreason-synthesise cycles, (4) parameter-efficient fine-tuning of TinyLlama-1.1B via Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA), and (5) a Hybrid approach combining all three retrieval strategies to feed the fine-tuned model. Using TinyLlama\/TinyLlama-1.1B-Chat-v1.0 as the base model across all conditions, we evaluate each approach on five domain-relevant research questions using keyword-overlap relevance scoring and response-time measurement. The Multi-Step Agent achieved the highest average relevance score (0.88), followed by the Hybrid approach (0.67) and Fine-tuning (0.46), while vanilla RAG performed the worst on direct relevance despite lower latency. Our analysis identifies trade-offs between answer quality, computational cost, and deployment complexity, yielding practical guidance for researchers and practitioners selecting LLM augmentation strategies for knowledge-intensive tasks.<\/jats:p>","DOI":"10.2139\/ssrn.6691280","type":"posted-content","created":{"date-parts":[[2026,7,29]],"date-time":"2026-07-29T13:27:11Z","timestamp":1785331631000},"source":"Crossref","is-referenced-by-count":0,"title":["Comparative Evaluation of Large Language Model Augmentation Strategies: RAG, Knowledge Graph, Multi-Step Agent, Fine-Tuning, and Hybrid Approaches"],"prefix":"10.2139","author":[{"ORCID":"https:\/\/orcid.org\/0009-0001-6547-1650","authenticated-orcid":true,"given":"Hari Prasad","family":"Sampatirao","sequence":"first","affiliation":[],"role":[{"vocabulary":"crossref","role":"author"}]}],"member":"78","deposited":{"date-parts":[[2026,7,29]],"date-time":"2026-07-29T13:27:11Z","timestamp":1785331631000},"score":59.9923,"resource":{"primary":{"URL":"https:\/\/www.ssrn.com\/abstract=6691280"}},"issued":{"date-parts":[[2026]]},"references-count":0,"URL":"https:\/\/doi.org\/10.2139\/ssrn.6691280","published":{"date-parts":[[2026]]},"subtype":"preprint"},{"indexed":{"date-parts":[[2024,9,5]],"date-time":"2024-09-05T00:39:28Z","timestamp":1725496768041},"posted":{"date-parts":[[2024,9,4]]},"group-title":"Open Science Framework","reference-count":0,"publisher":"Center for Open Science","license":[{"start":{"date-parts":[[2024,9,4]],"date-time":"2024-09-04T00:00:00Z","timestamp":1725408000000},"content-version":"unspecified","delay-in-days":0,"URL":"https:\/\/creativecommons.org\/licenses\/by\/4.0\/legalcode"}],"content-domain":{"domain":[],"crossmark-restriction":false},"abstract":"

Rapid advancements in artificial intelligence have led to the widespread deployment of language models across various domains, from customer service to content generation, where the generation of accurate and ethically sound responses is paramount. Addressing the dual challenges of toxic content generation and the need for sophisticated reasoning, this research introduces a novel approach that integrates targeted pruning techniques to enhance multi-hop reasoning while simultaneously reducing the presence of toxic knowledge. By fine-tuning the pre-trained Llama model, the study explores how selective pruning of toxic pathways can improve the model's accuracy, response diversity, and robustness against adversarial prompts. The findings reveal that pruning not only mitigates harmful content but also significantly enhances the model's reasoning capabilities, demonstrating a meaningful reduction in Average Toxicity Score and an increase in Exact Match and F1 scores. Through a combination of empirical evaluations and robust analysis, the study provides evidence that strategic pruning serves as an effective tool for aligning the ethical and functional performance of language models. This research highlights the potential for pruning techniques to contribute to the development of more reliable, safe, and ethically aligned artificial intelligence systems, ensuring that they meet both societal standards and practical requirements in diverse BV","content-domain":{"domain":[],"crossmark-restriction":false},"abstract":"With the rapid development of multimodal artificial intelligence, integrating heterogeneous evidence from text and vision has become a fundamental challenge in knowledge-guided reasoning, intelligent decision support, and information analysis in high-stakes scenarios. However, cross-modal evidence understanding still faces three persistent obstacles. First, there remains a substantial gap between low-level perceptual signals and domain semantics. Existing visual models are often effective at recognizing physical objects, local attributes, and spatial layouts. However, they frequently fail to determine the evidential meaning, functional role, and task relevance of these observations without domain knowledge and contextual cues. As a result, visually similar objects may correspond to very different evidence entities, while small but critical evidence items may be ignored because they are not visually salient. Second, there is a pronounced mismatch between abstract textual descriptions and complex visual scenes. Textual evidence is often expressed at the event level, relation level, or role level, whereas visual evidence is distributed across fine grained entities, local regions, occluded targets, and cluttered backgrounds. This mismatch makes direct one to one alignment unreliable, especially when crucial evidence is weakly visible, partially hidden, or embedded in dense scene context. Third, high quality benchmark resources remain scarce in privacy sensitive domains. Real world evidence data are difficult to access, difficult to release, and expensive to annotate with fine grained cross modal correspondences, which limits not only model training but also fair comparison and reproducible evaluation. To address these challenges, this study proposes a knowledge-guided framework for cross modal evidence entity alignment. First, we design a logical reconstruction pipeline and construct EviMM, a high fidelity and privacy preserving multimodal evidence dataset with fine grained alignment annotations. Second, we propose EviGraph-Align, a two stage framework that injects domain semantics into multimodal representations and performs coarse to fine candidate matching under graph structured context. Third, we develop an evidence verification mechanism that uses structural neighbor consistency to eliminate visually salient but semantically irrelevant distractors in cluttered scenes. Experimental results show that domain semantic injection and graph-based contextual reranking substantially improve alignment quality and effectively bridge the gap between perceptual observations and domain semantics.
